chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, peace be upon them, who said:

Two men entered the mosque while Ali (peace be upon him) had already led the people in prayer, so he said to them: 'If you wish, one of you may lead the other in prayer, and he should not call the adhan nor call the iqamah.'
And it is appropriate that he calls the adhan behind whoever is reciting behind him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on leading a prayer for two people who enter late after the Imam has finished?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the flexibility of congregational prayer (*Salat al-Jama'ah*) when two individuals enter after the Imam has concluded, allowing one to lead the other without the formalities of *adhan* or *iqamah*. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for the follower to recite the *adhan* behind the leader, reflecting a nuanced approach to maintaining the spirit of congregation even in informal settings. This ruling underscores the practical adaptability of prayer rituals in early Islamic communities as recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi.
